light-bands: At fixed wave speed, how far must one crest travel before the next crest passes the same point?
Which quantity does “in a vacuum” fix for light? Check that before changing its speed.
rays-wavefronts: Draw two straight, tilted fronts. What direction would arrows perpendicular to both fronts have?
Check the angle between the old ray and the newly tilted fronts.
ray-validity: In wavelength ÷ opening width, which number is in the denominator?
Compare the opening size with a single wavelength. Is the opening still large enough to ignore spreading?
intensity-area: Draw equal squares inside the original detector. How many are still collecting light?
Irradiance is power per area. What else do you need for total power?
reflection-normal: The normal is drawn at right angles to the mirror. From which line are you measuring?
Sketch the incoming ray and its mirror image about the normal. Which angle would 50° describe?
snell-index: Draw a front arriving squarely at the boundary. Which side would enter the glass first?
Count crests arriving at a fixed point on the boundary each second. Does the boundary create extra crests?
total-internal: Which material was the ray leaving in the worked critical-angle example?
Test a ray entering straight along the normal. What would prevent transmission at that angle?
dispersion-colour: In the refraction rule, do the two colors have the same index as well as the same incoming angle?
For the same incoming ray, compare the angle that goes with a larger index in Snell’s rule.
real-virtual: Trace a real light ray from the mirror to the location of the proposed screen.
The screen color changes what it reflects. What light actually reaches the back of the mirror?
mirror-curvature: Put the focal length and the object distance into the mirror equation with their signs. What happens when you move the object term across the equals sign?
Sketch two reflected rays from a convex mirror. Do they head toward one another in front of it?
thin-lens-signs: Put the stated distances into 1/image distance = 1/f − 1/object distance before inverting.
Is zero reciprocal distance the same as zero distance? Try the reciprocal of an increasingly large number.
magnification-sign: Use the minus sign in m = −image distance/object distance together with the sign of the image distance.
Which distance goes in the numerator of the magnification rule?
two-lens-trace: Draw the location the rays from lens 1 are heading toward. On which side of lens 2 is it?
Put a new zero at lens 2. What is the distance from that new zero to the first image?
stops-pupils: Which clue describes a loss of scene area, and which would describe a loss of colors?
Trace rays from the centre and then the edge. Which group does this device mostly remove?
camera-focus: Even a perfectly focused point spreads when it passes through a tiny opening. What sets the width of that spot?
Try distinguishing the number of arriving photons from the width of the pattern each helps build.
optical-instruments: In the angular magnification ratio, does the eyepiece focal length multiply or divide?
Write both focal lengths in the ratio. Which of the two has just changed?
field-components: Draw the old and new field arrows on a grid and compare their lengths.
Keep the signed vertical coordinate when plotting the tip. Is it in the same quadrant?
analyzer-angle: After the middle filter, what is the polarization of light arriving at the last filter?
At each filter compare the incoming field with the angle of that filter. Does a nonzero part passing through require extra energy?
circular-ellipse: Compare the farthest horizontal and vertical positions reached by the tip. A circle requires what relation?
At a quarter-cycle offset, do the horizontal and vertical parts reach their peaks simultaneously?
wave-plate: A wave plate adds a delay between two parts. How many nonzero input parts are present here?
What two nonzero field components are required to trace a circle?
field-not-intensity: Compare the sizes of the two field amplitudes before combining them. Equal opposite signs alone are not enough.
For beams with a fixed phase difference, do you add their intensities or their signed field amplitudes first?
optical-path: One whole wavelength spans one whole turn of phase. How much of a turn does this extra path cover?
Which quantity sets the timing of the crests, the endpoints alone or the optical distance traveled?
two-slit-spacing: Write fringe spacing as wavelength × screen distance ÷ slit separation. Which input changed?
Compare the position of wavelength in the fringe-spacing rule with the position of slit separation.
coherence-visibility: Write visibility as a difference divided by a sum. How does doubling both readings affect the denominator?
Track the factor of two in the numerator as well as in the denominator.
michelson-double-path: Trace the beam from the splitter to the moving mirror and back. How many legs change length?
Does the mirror need to move a whole wavelength for the complete round trip to change by one wavelength?
reflection-phase: Separate the sign of a reflected field from the power carried by that field.
How do you turn the signed amplitude reflection factor into a power fraction?
thin-film-condition: List the phase change on each reflection again. Which difference between beams controls reinforcement?
Two reflected waves still meet. Which part of their timing changed when the substrate changed?
phase-ambiguity: Imagine a clock hand that has returned to its starting mark. Can you tell how many complete turns it made?
Can the phase sensor count whole cycles using only its starting and finishing readings?
huygens-front: Do the contributions from two points on an opening always arrive in step at the detector?
Compare light at one dark direction with the total light that gets through the entire opening.
single-aperture: In the small-angle rule, is slit width above or below the division sign?
Which width determines the path difference between light from opposite edges?
finite-double-slit: Match slit width and slit separation to their different patterns. Which quantity changed in this setup?
The difference in travel distance from the two slit centres depends on which length?
grating-orders: Write the grating condition for the same groove spacing and the same angle. What product remains to compare?
Include the order number when comparing the two wavelengths.
point-spread: Moving a source shifts its spot. Does the aperture that shapes each individual spot change?
Did either source produce extra power, or did their spots just move closer?
angular-resolution: Check the location of wavelength in the ratio wavelength ÷ aperture diameter.
With diameter fixed, compare the two wavelengths in the diffraction rule.
numerical-aperture: Look at the two factors in NA = index × sine of the angle. Where would wavelength enter?
How large can the sine factor become, even for a very wide collecting cone?
sampling-contrast: Try a pattern already blurred into one spot by the lens. What does a finer pixel grid sample?
If a good optical image lands between widely spaced pixels, what might finer spacing recover?
spatial-frequency: Draw a stripe pattern three times wider with the same number of stripes. How many stripes fit per centimetre?
The question counts stripes per unit length in an image. Does it count light cycles per second?
far-field-transform: Pick a direction where two parts used to reinforce. Would a changed phase at one part matter there?
What information is lost when a complex field is replaced by its squared size?
frequency-filter: Which quantity is the filter transferring in each case, the field or the intensity?
Two beams can have the same brightness and different timing. Which of those features matters in coherent imaging?
near-far: Write the Fresnel number as a squared width divided by wavelength times distance. Where does distance occur?
Mark all three quantities in the Fresnel number before holding any of them fixed.
absorption-law: What power arrives at the second slab after the first slab?
The second slab removes half of what reaches it. Is that the same amount the first slab removed?
guided-modes: The index check gives a range. What must the wave also do at the guide’s edges?
Compare a narrow guide with a wide guide. Which boundary distances have changed?
detector-shot-noise: For counting noise, compare the square root of the count with the count itself. They grow at different rates.
The exposure now produces four times as many events. Which changes faster, the count or its square root?
photon-energy: The medium and frequency still match the old beam. What in the wavelength rule has changed?
Use energy per photon = Planck’s constant × frequency. Then account for the extra energy arriving each second.
choose-optical-model: Two equal-power beams can meet crest to crest or crest to trough. What distinguishes those situations?
A lens can aim the beams at a place. What makes them cancel once they get there?
system-capstone: Draw the two lenses on one distance axis and mark the zero used for each image distance.
Changing image orientation changes its sign of magnification. Does that move the distance origin?
aperture-wavelength: Treat collection and diffraction separately. Where does diameter appear in the angular rule?
Sketch a circle three times wider. How many equal squares fit compared with the original area?
optics-assessment: Moving the detector does not reshape the lens. What changed in the detector’s position relative to the image?
Is the light’s frequency changing, or is the detector sampling a different slice of the converging beam?
